sections.heading: Purpose
Authority
sections.body_text:
This Code is adopted pursuant to:
1. Delegated Authority. Resolutions, directives, delegations, and other lawful actions of the Board of Directors, Chief Executive Officer, or other duly authorized Company officials.
2. Applicable Requirements. Applicable federal, state, and local law; contractual obligations; licenses and permits; regulatory requirements; financing arrangements; insurance requirements; and other obligations binding upon the Company.
In the event of a conflict, controlling law and the Company’s governing documents shall prevail, followed by duly adopted Board actions, this Code, Board Policies, executive directives, departmental policies, and subordinate administrative procedures, in that order unless a governing instrument expressly provides otherwise.

sections.heading: Applicability
Definitions
sections.body_text:
For purposes of this Code:
Administrative Directive — A written instruction issued by an authorized official to implement or administer authority established by law, governing documents, Board action, this Code, or Company policy.
Authorized Official — An officer, department head, manager, employee, or other person possessing authority by virtue of governing documents, Board action, this Code, written delegation, or other lawful authorization.
Board — The Board of Governors of Blevins Holdings LLC.
Board Policy / BP — A policy formally adopted or approved under authority specifically reserved to the Board.
Code — The Blevins Holdings Administrative Code.
Company — Blevins Holdings LLC.
Controlled Subsidiary — An entity for which Blevins Holdings directly or indirectly possesses the authority to control governance, management, or material operating decisions.
Department — An organizational unit of Blevins Holdings established by the Board, Chief Executive Officer, organizational plan, or other competent authority.
Department Head — The officer, executive, director, or other person designated to exercise administrative responsibility for a department.
Executive Directive — An enterprise-wide administrative instruction issued under executive authority.
General Counsel — The attorney designated or retained by the Company to serve as its General Counsel, including the Contracted General Counsel when applicable.
OIG — The Office of Inspector General or equivalent internal oversight function of Blevins Holdings.
Policy — A formally approved statement establishing mandatory principles, standards, requirements, or controls.
Procedure — Documented instructions prescribing how a policy, rule, requirement, or administrative function is to be carried out.
Record — Recorded information, regardless of medium or format, created, received, maintained, or controlled in connection with Company business.
Subsidiary — A legal entity directly or indirectly owned or controlled by Blevins Holdings.

sections.heading: Rules of Construction
sections.body_text:
Unless the context requires otherwise:
1. Words in the singular include the plural and words in the plural include the singular.
2. “Shall” and “must” establish a mandatory requirement.
3. “May” grants discretion or authority but does not impose a mandatory duty.
4. “Including” means including without limitation.
5. References to a department include any successor department assigned substantially equivalent responsibilities.
6. References to a law, regulation, policy, standard, or other authority include amendments and successor provisions.
7. Headings are for organization and convenience and do not independently limit substantive requirements.
8. A specific provision controls over a general provision concerning the same subject.
9. Duties assigned by this Code may be delegated unless delegation is prohibited by law, governing documents, Board action, or this Code.

sections.heading: Severability
sections.body_text: If any provision of this Code or its application is determined to be invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in effect to the maximum extent permitted.

sections.heading: No Creation of Employment or Third-Party Rights
Code Administrator
Official Version
sections.body_text:
The version maintained in the Company’s designated official policy or records repository shall constitute the authoritative administrative copy of this Code.
Unofficial reproductions, extracts, summaries, or copies shall not supersede the official version.

sections.heading: Administrative Interpretation
sections.body_text:
Questions concerning interpretation shall ordinarily be resolved by the responsible department in consultation with the Code Administrator.
Questions involving legal authority, interpretation of governing documents, regulatory requirements, legal privilege, or material legal risk shall be referred to the General Counsel.

sections.heading: Amendments
sections.body_text:
This Code may be amended by:
1. The Board;
2. The Chief Executive Officer acting within delegated authority; or
3. Another official expressly authorized to amend specified provisions.
No administrative amendment may modify, impair, or circumvent authority reserved to the Board or established by controlling law or governing documents.

sections.heading: Technical Corrections
Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish the administrative organization of Blevins Holdings and provide for assignment of enterprise functions.

sections.heading: Authority
sections.body_text: This Chapter is adopted pursuant to the Company’s governing documents, organizational authority of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, approved organizational plans, and applicable law.

sections.heading: Divisions
sections.body_text:
The administrative organization of Blevins Holdings may include the following divisions and organizational functions:
1. Administrative Operations (ADM)
2. Enterprise Operations (OPS)
3. Finance (FIN)
4. Revenue and Client Services (RCS)
5. Legal, Risk, and Compliance (LRC)
6. Office of Inspector General (OIG)
7. Communications and Public Affairs (COM)
8. Information Systems and Technology (IST)
9. Global Human Resources (GHR)
10. Subsidiaries (SUBSIDIARIES)
The Board or Chief Executive Officer, within their respective authority, may establish, consolidate, reorganize, rename, or discontinue departments and subordinate organizational units.

sections.heading: Divisional Heads
Organizational Charts
sections.body_text:
Administrative Operations or another designated function shall maintain the official enterprise organizational chart.
No organizational chart alone shall create authority exceeding that established by governing documents, Board action, this Code, or written delegation.
Chapter 4. Delegation of Authority

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Article is to establish uniform requirements for delegating administrative and approval authority.

sections.heading: General Rule
Written Delegations
Contents of Delegation
Responsibility Retained
sections.body_text: Delegation of authority does not relieve the delegating official of supervisory responsibility unless the governing authority expressly provides otherwise.

sections.heading: Prohibition on Self-Approval
sections.body_text: No person may approve a transaction, payment, reimbursement, personnel action, access request, or other matter in which that person is the requesting party or principal beneficiary when an independent approval is required.

sections.heading: Acting Officials
sections.body_text:
An acting official may exercise the duties and authority of the position for which the official is formally designated, subject to limitations in the acting designation, governing documents, or applicable law.
Chapter 5. Administrative Issuances

sections.heading: Authorized Issuances
Hierarchy
Policy Ownership
Exceptions
Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish minimum standards for financial stewardship, accounting, budgeting, treasury activities, expenditures, and internal financial control.

sections.heading: Financial Administration
sections.body_text: The Finance Department shall administer enterprise financial operations subject to Board-approved budgets, financial policies, delegations of authority, and applicable accounting and legal requirements.

sections.heading: Books and Records
Budget Administration
sections.body_text:
Departments shall operate within approved budgets and applicable spending authority.
Material budget transfers, unbudgeted expenditures, capital expenditures, and commitments extending beyond approved authority shall receive approval in accordance with applicable financial policy and delegation matrices.

sections.heading: Segregation of Duties
Reconciliations
sections.body_text:
Material financial accounts shall be reconciled at intervals appropriate to their risk and volume.
Material discrepancies shall be investigated and resolved promptly.

sections.heading: Expense Reimbursement
sections.body_text:
Company funds may reimburse legitimate, reasonable, documented business expenses in accordance with applicable policy.
No person may approve the person’s own reimbursement except through an expressly authorized independent review process.
Chapter 7. Procurement and Contract Administration

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish fair, controlled, and commercially reasonable procedures for acquisition of goods and services.

sections.heading: Procurement Standards
Competitive Sourcing
Contract Review
sections.body_text: Contracts shall receive legal, financial, security, privacy, risk, procurement, or other functional review when required by policy or the nature of the transaction.

sections.heading: Contract Signature
sections.body_text:
No employee or agent may bind the Company to a contract unless the person possesses sufficient delegated signature authority.
Use of Company letterhead, email, purchasing systems, or job title does not independently create contracting authority.

sections.heading: Vendor Due Diligence
Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish uniform administrative standards for personnel management.

sections.heading: Administration
sections.body_text: Global Human Resources shall establish and administer enterprise personnel standards consistent with applicable law, Board Policy, executive direction, compensation authority, and approved workforce plans.

sections.heading: Personnel Actions
Personnel Records
sections.body_text: Personnel records shall be maintained with appropriate confidentiality, access controls, retention requirements, and legal protections.

sections.heading: Conflicts of Interest
sections.body_text:
Employees and officials shall disclose actual or reasonably apparent conflicts of interest in accordance with Company policy.
No employee may participate in a Company decision where an undisclosed personal or financial interest materially impairs, or reasonably appears to impair, independent business judgment.
Chapter 9. Records and Information Governance

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish standards for creation, classification, preservation, retention, access, protection, and disposition of Company records.

sections.heading: Ownership
sections.body_text: Records created or received in the course of Company business are Company property unless otherwise provided by law or contract.

sections.heading: Records Retention
sections.body_text:
Records shall be retained and disposed of according to an approved records retention schedule.
Records subject to a legal hold, investigation hold, audit hold, regulatory preservation requirement, or other preservation directive shall not be altered, destroyed, or disposed of until the hold is released.

sections.heading: Official Repositories
sections.body_text:
Departments shall use designated systems of record for official Company information when such systems have been established.
Material Company records shall not be maintained solely in personal accounts, unauthorized applications, or other locations outside Company control.

sections.heading: Confidential Information
sections.body_text:
Access to confidential or restricted information shall be limited to persons with an authorized business need.
Confidential information shall be handled in accordance with applicable data-classification, privacy, legal, security, contractual, and records-management requirements.
Chapter 10. Information Systems and Technology

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish administrative governance for Company information systems, technology assets, cybersecurity controls, data, and technology services.

sections.heading: Administration
sections.body_text: Information Systems and Technology shall administer enterprise technology standards, architecture, infrastructure, access controls, cybersecurity requirements, technology procurement standards, and approved technology services.

sections.heading: Authorized Systems
sections.body_text: Company information shall be processed, stored, transmitted, or accessed only through authorized systems when required by Company policy.

sections.heading: Access Control
Security Incidents
sections.body_text: Suspected or confirmed cybersecurity incidents, unauthorized access, material data loss, malware, compromise of credentials, or unauthorized disclosure of protected information shall be promptly reported through designated incident-response channels.

sections.heading: Technology Changes
sections.body_text: Material changes to production systems shall be subject to appropriate testing, authorization, documentation, segregation of duties, rollback planning, and change-management controls proportionate to risk.

sections.heading: Artificial Intelligence and Automated Systems
Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish administrative standards for Company facilities, physical assets, workplace operations, and business continuity.

sections.heading: Facilities Administration
sections.body_text: Administrative Operations and Enterprise Operations shall coordinate the management of Company facilities and enterprise operational services according to assigned responsibilities.

sections.heading: Physical Access
sections.body_text:
Access to controlled Company facilities shall be based upon legitimate business need and applicable physical-security requirements.
Access credentials remain Company property and may not be shared, duplicated, or transferred except as expressly authorized.

sections.heading: Company Property
Business Continuity
sections.body_text:
Departments responsible for critical operations shall maintain continuity and recovery arrangements proportionate to operational risk.
T I T L E 5 Legal, Risk, Compliance, and Oversight
Chapter 12. Legal Affairs

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish standards for legal representation, legal review, privilege, litigation, claims, and legal-risk management.

sections.heading: General Counsel
Engagement of Outside Counsel
sections.body_text: No department may independently engage outside legal counsel at Company expense except as authorized by the General Counsel, Chief Executive Officer, Board, or applicable policy.

sections.heading: Legal Privilege
sections.body_text:
Communications with counsel shall be handled in a manner designed to preserve applicable attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, and confidentiality.
Privileged material shall not be distributed beyond persons with a legitimate need without authorization from Legal.

sections.heading: Legal Process
sections.body_text:
Subpoenas, summonses, warrants, regulatory demands, litigation notices, formal claims, and other legal process received by Company personnel shall be promptly referred to Legal in accordance with established procedures.
Chapter 13. Risk and Compliance

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish an enterprise framework for compliance with legal, regulatory, contractual, ethical, and policy requirements.

sections.heading: Compliance Responsibility
sections.body_text:
Compliance is a responsibility shared by all Company personnel.
The Legal, Risk, and Compliance Department shall coordinate enterprise compliance activities, subject to oversight by executive management and the Board.

sections.heading: Compliance Program
Mandatory Reporting
sections.body_text: Personnel shall promptly report known or reasonably suspected material violations of law, fraud, corruption, theft, significant conflicts of interest, serious policy violations, retaliation, material cybersecurity incidents, or other conduct required to be reported under Company policy.

sections.heading: Non-Retaliation
sections.body_text:
Retaliation against a person for making a good-faith report, participating in an authorized investigation, or raising a compliance concern is prohibited.
This section does not prevent appropriate action concerning knowingly false statements, bad-faith misconduct, or independent violations of Company requirements.

sections.heading: Corrective Action
Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish the Office of Inspector General as an internal oversight function responsible for promoting integrity, accountability, efficiency, and appropriate stewardship of Company resources.

sections.heading: Functions
Access
sections.body_text: Personnel shall provide OIG timely access to Company records, systems, facilities, property, and personnel reasonably necessary to perform authorized work, subject to applicable legal restrictions and appropriate treatment of privileged material.

sections.heading: Independence
sections.body_text:
No person may improperly obstruct, interfere with, manipulate, or retaliate in connection with an authorized OIG review or investigation.
OIG shall maintain sufficient functional independence to report material matters through channels established by its charter or Board Policy.

sections.heading: Cooperation
sections.body_text:
Employees, officers, departments, and controlled subsidiaries shall cooperate with authorized OIG activities.
Nothing in this section requires waiver of attorney-client privilege, work-product protection, or other legally protected rights.
T I T L E 6 Enterprise and Subsidiary Governance
Chapter 15. Subsidiary Administration

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish enterprise governance standards for entities owned or controlled by Blevins Holdings.

sections.heading: Covered Subsidiaries
Separate Legal Existence
sections.body_text:
Each subsidiary shall observe its separate legal existence, governing documents, capitalization requirements, books and records, contractual obligations, regulatory requirements, and corporate formalities.
Nothing in this Code authorizes disregard of legal separateness between Blevins Holdings and any subsidiary.

sections.heading: Reserved Matters
Enterprise Policies
Subsidiary Reporting
Shared Services
Intercompany Arrangements
sections.body_text: Material intercompany services, loans, transfers, intellectual-property licenses, cost allocations, guarantees, and other intercompany arrangements shall be documented when required by law, accounting standards, tax requirements, financing arrangements, or Company policy.

sections.heading: Conflicts Among Enterprise Entities
sections.body_text:
Material conflicts between departments or subsidiaries shall be escalated through the applicable management chain.
Legal conflicts, fiduciary concerns, or matters involving potentially adverse interests among Company entities shall be referred to the General Counsel for appropriate handling, including consideration of separate counsel where warranted.
T I T L E 7 External Communications and Representation
Chapter 17. Communications and Public Affairs

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body_text: The purpose of this Chapter is to establish standards for official Company communications and representation.

sections.heading: Authorized Spokespersons
sections.body_text: Only persons authorized by Communications and Public Affairs, executive management, the Board, or applicable policy may speak on behalf of the Company to news media or issue official public statements.

sections.heading: Government and Regulatory Communications
sections.body_text: Official communications with governmental or regulatory bodies shall be coordinated with Legal, Compliance, Government Affairs, or other responsible functions when required by policy or circumstances.

sections.heading: Public Disclosures
sections.body_text:
Public disclosure of confidential, proprietary, privileged, nonpublic financial,
security-sensitive, personal, or — other restricted information is prohibited except as authorized or
legally required.

sections.heading: Brand and Identity
sections.body_text:
Use of Company names, trademarks, logos, official seals, letterhead, domains, and other identifiers shall comply with applicable brand and authorization standards.
T I T L E 8 Accountability and Enforcement
Chapter 18. Administrative Compliance

sections.heading: Duty to Comply
sections.body_text: Persons subject to this Code shall comply with its applicable provisions and with lawful directives issued under it.

sections.heading: Supervisory Responsibility
Violations
sections.body_text: A violation of this Code may constitute grounds for administrative, contractual, disciplinary, financial, or other corrective action, subject to applicable law and Company policy.

sections.heading: Reporting Violations
Investigation Authority
sections.body_text:
The Company may investigate suspected violations through an appropriately authorized department or external professional.
Investigations shall be conducted with due regard for confidentiality, legal privilege, fairness, evidence preservation, and applicable law.
Chapter 19. Waivers and Exceptions

sections.heading: General Rule
Temporary Exceptions
Emergency Action
Effective Date
sections.body_text: This Administrative Code shall take effect on the date established by the adopting authority.

sections.heading: Existing Policies and Procedures
sections.body_text:
Policies, procedures, directives, delegations, and
other
administrative instruments in effect immediately before adoption of this Code shall remain in effect to the extent they:
1. Are not inconsistent with this Code;
2. Have not expired;
3. Have not been superseded; and
4. Were issued by competent authority.

sections.heading: Conflicting Administrative Instruments
sections.body_text:
Departments shall identify
existing administrative
instruments that conflict with this Code and shall revise, repeal, or escalate those instruments for resolution.

sections.heading: Continuing Authority
sections.body_text: Adoption of this Code does not terminate lawful delegations, appointments, contracts, policies, procedures, or administrative actions unless expressly stated.

sections.heading: Periodic Review
Citation
sections.body_text:
This Code may be cited as the “Blevins Holdings Administrative Code” or “BHAC.” Individual provisions may be cited in substantially the following form:
BHAC § 3.24
